subject: Business
title: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy
description: A 60-second lesson on Good Strategy, Bad Strategy.

hook.text: Most 'strategies' are just goals wearing a costume. 'Grow 20%' is an aspiration, not a strategy.

buildup.text: Richard Rumelt says good strategy has three parts: a diagnosis, a guiding policy, and coherent actions.

discovery.text: Bad strategy avoids hard choices. It lists goals without explaining how to achieve them.

twist.text: Companies with five 'top priorities' have no priorities. Strategy requires painful trade-offs.

climax.text: Apple in 1997 killed 70% of its products. That painful cut was the strategy that saved the company.

punchline.text: If your strategy doesn't hurt, it's probably not a strategy.

quiz.question: According to Rumelt, what makes a strategy 'bad'?
options: It lists goals without explaining how to achieve them or making trade-offs
It focuses on a single objective

details.summary: Richard Rumelt distinguishes good strategy from bad by identifying three elements of good strategy: a diagnosis of the challenge, a guiding policy for dealing with it, and coherent actions to execute the policy.
details.whyItMatters: Most organizations mistake goals for strategy. Saying we will be number one is not a strategy. Rumelt's framework helps leaders identify whether they have a genuine strategy with a clear theory of competitive advantage or just wishful thinking.
takeaways: Good strategy has a diagnosis, guiding policy, and coherent action plan
Bad strategy substitutes aspirations and goals for genuine strategic choices
Strategy requires saying no to attractive alternatives to focus resources

faq.question: What makes most corporate strategies bad strategies?
faq.answer: They list goals without explaining how to achieve them. They refuse to make hard choices about what not to do. They use fluffy language and buzzwords instead of clear analysis. They fail to identify the specific challenge the strategy must address. They are wish lists, not strategies.

faq.question: What is the strategic kernel that defines good strategy?
faq.answer: The kernel has three parts. A diagnosis that simplifies reality by identifying the critical challenge. A guiding policy that specifies the approach to addressing the challenge. Coherent actions that are coordinated and focused to implement the guiding policy. All three must align.
